answer.evidence: The top part (rows 0-9) is a sign box seen face-on. Its white face (rows 1-7) carries a centered symbol and shows no front-edge line. Rows 8-9 are a teal band on the face, not a receding surface. The right side is shaded teal like a vertical side. The silhouette is 6, 12, then 14 across rows 2-8, then 12 at row 9 and 10 for the shaft. That is a chamfered box with squared-off sides, not an ellipse plate that overhangs and narrows both above and below. The shaft (rows 10-25) is a flat vertical tan panel with the '3' and no top or edge line. The base (rows 26-30) is a flared foot, also a vertical face. No part of the object shows a horizontal top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bollard-style exit-number sign: a grey cylindrical post with a cap and a lit number panel. It carries 11 visible tones per 16x16 tile, close to kiosk-a (12) and above bus-shelter-a (6), though below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so it has no large flat fills, where bus-shelter-a has 9%. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted, a dark blue-grey beside the grey body, matching the references. The body shows a highlight and shadow side with about 4 steps, a bit fewer than the 5 or so on the kiosk and vending references. Its shading is comparable to the shipped modern_city props, and it would not look thinner or flatter beside them.
